:::{#exm-cross-product-sum-outer}
#### The Gram matrix and a cross-product as sums of outer products

Let $\matr{A} = \sbmat{1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1}$,
$\matr{B} = \sbmat{1 \\ 2 \\ 3}$
be the matrices of @exm-cross-product-matrix.
The rows of $\matr{A}$ are $\vecf{r}_1 = (1, 0)$, $\vecf{r}_2 = (1, 1)$, $\vecf{r}_3 = (0, 1)$.
Taking $\matr{B} = \matr{A}$ in @thm-cross-product-sum-outer,
the [Gram matrix](#def-gram-matrix) is the [sum](algebra.qmd#def-summation) of the [outer products](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-outer-product) of the rows with themselves:

$$
\ba
\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{A}}
&= \vecf{r}_1\,\tp{\vecf{r}_1} + \vecf{r}_2\,\tp{\vecf{r}_2} + \vecf{r}_3\,\tp{\vecf{r}_3}
&& \text{(@thm-cross-product-sum-outer)}
\\
&= \sbmat{1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0}
+ \sbmat{1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1}
+ \sbmat{0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1}
&& \text{(@def-outer-product)}
\\
&= \sbmat{2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2}.
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

This is the Gram matrix of @exm-gram-matrix.
Now keep the column $\matr{B}$ above.
Its rows are the 1-vectors $\vecf{s}_1 = (1)$, $\vecf{s}_2 = (2)$, $\vecf{s}_3 = (3)$, so

$$
\ba
\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}
&= 1 \vecf{r}_1 + 2 \vecf{r}_2 + 3 \vecf{r}_3
&& \text{(@thm-cross-product-sum-outer)}
\\
&= \sbmat{1 \\ 0}
+ \sbmat{2 \\ 2}
+ \sbmat{0 \\ 3}
&& \text{(scalar multiples)}
\\
&= \sbmat{3 \\ 5},
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

the same as in @exm-cross-product-matrix.

:::
